originalPrompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a highly legible, realistic, implementable Windows desktop application DESIGN REFERENCE for DEPTH AI, a visual code module explorer. Landscape 16:10, straight-on complete app window, crisp UI text, all four panes simultaneously visible. Start fresh; no previous image reference. English app interface.

CRITICAL USER-SPECIFIED LAYOUT, DO NOT REARRANGE:
A compact 48px top toolbar, then EXACTLY FOUR persistent quadrants separated by actual thin draggable splitters.
LEFT column 53% of window, RIGHT column 47%.
UPPER row 65% of remaining height, LOWER row 35%.
TOP LEFT: large LIVE PROJECT PREVIEW, header "Project preview". A rendered checkout app occupies almost all this quadrant.
BOTTOM LEFT: "Console & Meta CLI". This entire quadrant is a useful terminal/chat WORKSPACE, not a decorative tiny status bar. Within it console output occupies the left third, Meta CLI conversation and a broad command entry occupy the right two thirds. BOTH console and chat are visible.
TOP RIGHT: "Module canvas", a genuine spatial module composition with connected typed module shapes and owner groups, NOT an ordinary file browser, NOT paragraph cards.
BOTTOM RIGHT: "Hierarchy & quick switch", a searchable code hierarchy and a compact recent module list, NOT replaced by source code or explanations.
NO full-window bottom code strip. NO external side bar. NO giant page heading. NO panel hides another. Left bottom MUST be console/chat; right bottom MUST be hierarchy.

VISUAL DISTINCTION: preview resembles a white application viewport with fine browser-like chrome; module canvas has a pale blue-gray drafting surface; console/chat is deep graphite with bright readable monospace text; hierarchy is a pale neutral tree/list with distinct indentation and small role symbols. Use a modern readable sans-serif, monospace only code/terminal. Function modules are broad chamfered plates, state/property modules are slim cylindrical register shapes, classes are open corner-bracket containers labeled with class name. Assets are thumbnail tiles. Use burnt orange only for selected preview item, selected method, and selected tree row; muted blue and sage for context. No perspective, no neon, no all-identical rounded cards, no overlapping lines/text. Big enough fonts to read at normal desktop scale. Role words plus shapes, not color alone.

CONTENT:
Top toolbar "DEPTH AI | Checkout" and compact "Inspect  Explain  Transform  Assets  Review", right "Light  Dark  Meta".
Preview: shopping basket with a ceramic mug at $48 and small indoor plant at $72, subtotal $120, Discount (20%) -$24, Total $96, coupon input and Apply coupon button. Total $96 has a thin orange selection frame, label "Selected: Total". Keep its entire app viewport visible above console.
Module canvas: multiple distinct owners, with real named methods and state: CheckoutController / ApplyCoupon; CouponValidator / IsValid; CouponRules / CalculateTotal and DiscountPercent=20; CartState / Subtotal=120, Total=96, SetTotal; TotalsView / Read; CartSummary / Estimate. CalculateTotal orange. Fine directed source relations through whitespace: ApplyCoupon -> IsValid, CalculateTotal, SetTotal, Read; Estimate -> CalculateTotal; CalculateTotal -> DiscountPercent. Ownership is indicated by open brackets, not call arrows. Compact role labels. Include Fit and +/- controls in the canvas header. At top of canvas a compact breadcrumb "Preview: Total > CalculateTotal" connects selection conceptually without drawing a huge arrow across splitters.
Bottom-left console pane shows only source/status-neutral sample logs: "> open Checkout", "workspace: Checkout", "> inspect Total". Meta CLI pane shows USER "Why does the total become 96?" and assistant concise "CalculateTotal applies the 20% discount to 120. Source: CouponRules.cs". Its bottom has a wide actual input row with "> Ask about the selected module..." and a Send arrow.
Bottom-right hierarchy header includes search "Find a module...". A clearly indented tree "Checkout" > "CheckoutController.cs" > CheckoutController > ApplyCoupon; another expanded "CouponRules.cs" > CouponRules > CalculateTotal (orange selected) and DiscountPercent; collapsed CartState.cs and depth.preview.json. A narrow recent list on the right has "Recent" / "CalculateTotal" / "ApplyCoupon" / "Read", with small role icons. Tree selection corresponds to selected graph method. Text must not overlap.
Tiny global footer "DESIGN REFERENCE". This is a design concept, do not claim actual test results or live API success. The four-pane topology is the most important requirement.
corrections:

Make these precise corrections:

workspace: Checkout
> inspect Total

3. Correct source connections in the TOP RIGHT module canvas. The only directed arrows permitted are:
ApplyCoupon -> IsValid
ApplyCoupon -> CalculateTotal
ApplyCoupon -> SetTotal
ApplyCoupon -> Read
Estimate -> CalculateTotal
CalculateTotal -> DiscountPercent

Place ApplyCoupon neutral blue, CalculateTotal alone burnt-orange as the selected method. Method plates have modest chamfered corners. State/property plates retain cylindrical register form. Preserve class labels and all existing modules including Subtotal and Total.
4. Keep selected Total 96 and matching CalculateTotal hierarchy row. Keep the entire console CLI input and hierarchy search visible. No other extra changes. Maintain small footer DESIGN REFERENCE.

Edit only the TOP RIGHT "Module canvas" pane of this screenshot design. Preserve the entire other three quadrants pixel-faithfully: the top-left checkout preview, bottom-left console AND Meta CLI, and bottom-right hierarchy and recent modules. Preserve the application toolbar and all panel sizes.

In the module canvas, simplify to an unambiguous SELECTED DEPENDENCY view. Keep all six owner groups and ALL existing named method/property bodies visible in their current approximate positions. Erase every existing connecting line between groups. Then draw ONLY these THREE connector arrows:
1. ApplyCoupon -> CalculateTotal: one thin orange horizontal connector routed through the whitespace below the top-row bodies; starts on ApplyCoupon body and ends with arrowhead at left side of CalculateTotal BODY.
2. Estimate -> CalculateTotal: one thin charcoal curved connector going to the RIGHT of the CouponRules group, starts on the right side of Estimate body, curves outside the right border of CouponRules, then ends with arrowhead on the RIGHT SIDE OF CalculateTotal BODY. It must NOT touch DiscountPercent or the group border.
3. CalculateTotal -> DiscountPercent: short vertical charcoal arrow from bottom of CalculateTotal body to top of DiscountPercent cylinder.
There must be NO other connecting lines anywhere in this pane. The other modules remain visible as context with no call arrows.
Make all function bodies visibly chamfered hexagonal plates, rather than rounded rectangle buttons; keep their readable names. Keep state bodies cylindrical.
Under the module-canvas header add a small caption "Selected links · all modules visible". Keep CalculateTotal the only orange module. Preserve the frame's DESIGN REFERENCE footer.
